idea-plugin.name: HTTP Status Code Inline Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Shows the official name of any HTTP status code (404 -> Not Found, 503 -> Service Unavailable) inline, right after the numeric literal, in Java and Kotlin code -- no need to look it up. Works in any code context, not tied to a specific HTTP framework's own annotations.

Only lights up in places with real HTTP signal: a call whose method name looks like status handling (setStatus(404), sendError(500)), an annotation like @ResponseStatus(404), or a comparison against something named like a status holder (statusCode == 404). An ordinary loop bound or an unrelated numeric literal that happens to match a real status code (for (i in 0..500)) never shows a hint -- see the plugin's README for the full heuristic and worked examples.

The status table is the real IANA HTTP Status Code Registry (RFC 9110 and related RFCs) -- a number that merely looks plausible (3 digits, in range) but isn't a registered code, like 499 or 250, never gets an invented name.

100% local -- no network call, no account, no telemetry.
